item.title: “Mahāli, there is a cause, a condition for the defilement of beings. Mahāli, there is a cause, a condition for the purification of beings.” “But,…
item.description:
“Mahāli, there is a cause, a condition for the defilement of beings. Mahāli, there is a cause, a condition for the purification of beings.” “But, venerable sir, what is the cause, what is the condition for the defilement of beings?” “Mahāli, if form were exclusively suffering, immersed in suffering, accompanied by suffering, not accompanied by happiness, beings would not become lustful for form. But because form is happiness, Mahāli, immersed in happiness, accompanied by happiness, not accompanied by suffering, beings become lustful for form. Through lust, they are bound; through being bound, they are defiled. This, Mahāli, is the cause, this is the condition for the defilement of beings. Such being the cause, such being the condition, beings are defiled.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.60

item.title: - “Venerable Bharadvāja, what is the cause, what is the reason why these young monks, youthful, with black hair, endowed with the blessing of youth,…
item.description:
- “Venerable Bharadvāja, what is the cause, what is the reason why these young monks, youthful, with black hair, endowed with the blessing of youth, in the prime of life, do not indulge in sensual pleasures and live the perfectly pure holy life for their whole life, completing it fully?” - “Great king, the Blessed One, the Knower, the Seer, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, has said: ‘Come, monks, regarding those who are like mothers, establish a mother’s mind. Regarding those who are like sisters, establish a sister’s mind. Regarding those who are like daughters, establish a daughter’s mind.’ This, great king, is the cause, this is the reason why these young monks … live the holy life completely.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 35.127

item.title: Having abandoned sensual desires in the world, Homeless, gone forth into renunciation, Having abandoned sensual desire and existence, That one I call a true brahmin.…
item.description:
Having abandoned sensual desires in the world,
Homeless, gone forth into renunciation,
Having abandoned sensual desire and existence,
That one I call a true brahmin.

Having abandoned greed and ill-will in the world,
Homeless, gone forth into renunciation,
Having abandoned ill-will and existence,
That one I call a true brahmin.

Who has abandoned the human yoke
And transcended the heavenly yoke,
Having abandoned all yokes,
Released from all bondage —
That one I call a true brahmin.

Having abandoned pleasure and displeasure,
Cooled, without substratum,
A hero who has conquered all worlds,
Mighty and courageous —
That one I call a true brahmin.

Who fully and truly knows
The passing away and rebirth of beings,
Not clinging, well-gone, awakened,
Attained to perfect enlightenment —
That one I call a true brahmin.

Who has no clinging to the past,
The future, or the present,
Not clinging, without possessions —
That one I call a true brahmin.

Who knows his former abodes,
Sees heavenly and evil destinations,
And has attained the destruction of birth —
That one I call a true brahmin.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 98 – Vāseṭṭhasutta
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Truly, brahmins, this world is led by aging, illness, and death. Since the world is led by aging, illness, and death, brahmins, restraint of body,…
item.description:
“Truly, brahmins, this world is led by aging, illness, and death. Since the world is led by aging, illness, and death, brahmins, restraint of body, speech, and mind in this life is a refuge, a cave, an island, a shelter, and a destination for one who has gone to death.”

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 3.51
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monk, ‘butcher’s knife’ is a synonym for the five strands of sensual pleasure; ‘lifting the butcher’s knife’ means abandoning these five strands of sensual pleasure.…
item.description:
“Monk, ‘butcher’s knife’ is a synonym for the five strands of sensual pleasure; ‘lifting the butcher’s knife’ means abandoning these five strands of sensual pleasure. ‘The wise man, taking the sword, dug up’ is the meaning. ‘Piece of meat’ is a synonym for delight and lust; ‘lifting the piece of meat’ means abandoning that delight and lust. ‘The wise man, taking the sword, dug up’ is the meaning. ‘Viper’ is a synonym for a monk who has destroyed the defilements; ‘let the viper be, do not touch the viper, pay homage to the viper’ is the meaning.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 23 – Vammikasutta

item.title: Like a newly decorated medicine box, This foul body is adorned for the occasion — Enough to fool a fool, But not one who seeks…
item.description:
Like a newly decorated medicine box,
This foul body is adorned for the occasion —
Enough to fool a fool,
But not one who seeks the far shore.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 82 – Raṭṭhapālasutta
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: The Blessed One replied to Piṅgiya: “Seeing the danger in all forms, Beings living heedlessly, Afflicted by forms — Therefore, Piṅgiya, do not be heedless.…
item.description:
The Blessed One replied to Piṅgiya:
“Seeing the danger in all forms,
Beings living heedlessly,
Afflicted by forms —
Therefore, Piṅgiya, do not be heedless.
Abandon forms so as not to come to birth again.

Seeing beings, human folk,
Falling into craving,
Burned by old age,
Overcome by old age —
Therefore, Piṅgiya, do not be heedless.
Abandon craving so as not to come to birth again.”

From: Sutta Nipāta 5.17
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Truly, monks, it is impossible that one could enjoy sensual pleasures apart from sensual pleasures, apart from sensual perceptions, apart from sensual thoughts.”
item.description:
“Truly, monks, it is impossible that one could enjoy sensual pleasures apart from sensual pleasures, apart from sensual perceptions, apart from sensual thoughts.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 22 – Alagaddūpamasutta

item.title: “Monks, there are these three unwholesome thoughts: sensual thought, ill-will thought, harmful thought. And these three unwholesome thoughts are abandoned without remainder in one whose…
item.description:
“Monks, there are these three unwholesome thoughts: sensual thought, ill-will thought, harmful thought. And these three unwholesome thoughts are abandoned without remainder in one whose mind is well established in the four foundations of mindfulness or who develops the signless concentration. Monks, develop the signless concentration well. When the signless concentration is developed and cultivated, it brings great fruit and great benefit.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 22.80

item.title: The eye is unguarded, The faculties are unrestrained — Flies will swarm Thoughts of craving. The monk becomes rotten, Filled with foul smells — Far,…
item.description:
The eye is unguarded,
The faculties are unrestrained —
Flies will swarm
Thoughts of craving.
The monk becomes rotten,
Filled with foul smells —
Far, far away is Nibbāna!
He meets with misfortune.
In village or forest,
If one’s self is not peaceful,
The fool, without wisdom,
Walking or standing, is full of flies.
But one endowed with virtue,
Delighting in tranquil wisdom,
Lives peacefully and happily —
All flies are destroyed.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 3.128
